tier_b.def: a spiritual practice you commit to for a fixed length of time, with rules
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'practice' when there is a vow, a count and an end date. 'Practice' sounds like a hobby you do when free.

tier_b.def: the person doing a sadhana
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'practitioner' when the person is bound by a vow, not just attending sessions.

tier_b.def: a full set number of mantra repetitions finished inside fixed rules and dates
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'challenge' or 'program' for a counted, vowed campaign. English has no word for a quota that is also a rite.

tier_b.def: a vow spoken out loud before you begin, naming what you will do and why
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'intention' or 'goal'. An intention is private and soft; a sankalpa is stated, dated and binding.

tier_b.def: formal initiation by a teacher that hands you the right to practise something
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'training'. Training gives skill; diksha gives permission and a transmission.

tier_b.def: the teacher who removes the dark, and who takes responsibility for you
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'mentor'. A mentor advises and walks away; a guru is tied to your outcome.

tier_b.def: the one form of the divine that a person personally chooses and loves
tier_b.when: No clean English. 'Chosen deity' is the nearest and it drops the love and the exclusivity.

tier_b.def: the specific living intelligence behind a mantra, a place or a force
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'god'. A devata is one addressable being with a job, not the whole idea of God.

tier_b.def: seeing what you revere, and being seen back by it
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'a visit' or 'a viewing'. Darshan is two-directional; looking is not.

tier_b.def: a sound formula that works through its sound, not its meaning
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'affirmation' or 'chant'. An affirmation persuades you; a mantra does not care whether you believe it.

tier_b.def: repeating a mantra a counted number of times
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'repetition' when a count is being kept. Japa without a number is not japa.

tier_b.def: an offering given into fire
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'ritual' or 'ceremony' when things are actually being surrendered into fire and not returned.

tier_b.def: fire treated as a living mouth that receives what you give it
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'fire' when the fire is the receiver, not the scenery.

tier_b.def: the heat you make by choosing hardship on purpose
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'discipline'. Discipline is the schedule; tapas is the burn, and the burn is the point.

tier_b.def: daily and non-negotiable; done because it is never not done
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'daily'. Daily is a frequency; nitya is a standing obligation.

tier_b.def: an action plus the trace it leaves behind in you
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'consequences'. Consequences happen outside; karma includes the act and the mark it leaves inside.

tier_b.def: the groove a repeated action cuts into the mind
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'habit'. The habit is the behaviour; the samskara is the imprint that makes the behaviour likely.

tier_b.def: the right thing for you in particular to do, given who and where you are
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'duty'. Duty is handed to you from outside; dharma is fitted to you.

tier_b.def: freedom from the whole cycle, not freedom from one problem
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'freedom' when you mean the final kind that ends the loop.

tier_b.def: the endless loop of wanting, getting, and wanting again
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'the rat race'. The rat race is a workplace; samsara is the mechanism, and quitting your job does not exit it.

tier_b.def: the convincing surface of the world that hides what is actually there
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'illusion'. An illusion is false; maya is real enough to live inside, just not final.

tier_b.def: nature as the active material that everything is made of and does
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'nature' when you mean the moving, doing stuff, as opposed to the one watching it.

tier_b.def: the still witness that watches and never acts
tier_b.when: The partner term to prakriti. 'Consciousness' is too broad; purusha is specifically the one who does nothing.

tier_b.def: the three qualities everything is made of: clear, restless, heavy
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'calm / driven / lazy'. These describe the material itself, and they apply equally to a meal, a room, a workday and a person.

tier_b.def: the feeling and sorting part of the mind, the one that reacts
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'mind' when you specifically mean the reacting part, not the deciding part.

tier_b.def: the inner feeling-state you hold while doing something
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'mood' or 'attitude'. Bhava is the flavour you deliberately bring, not the mood that happens to you.

tier_b.def: the life-force that moves with the breath
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'energy'. Prana is specifically the moving, breath-linked kind, not motivation or calories.

tier_b.def: a fixed hand or body position that seals something in place
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'gesture'. A gesture communicates to someone; a mudra does a job whether anyone sees it or not.

tier_b.def: a geometric diagram that holds a deity, treated as the deity itself
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'symbol' or 'diagram'. A symbol points at a thing; a yantra is the thing.

tier_b.def: the coiled force at the base of the spine that can rise
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'awakening'. Kundalini names the force; awakening only names the event.

tier_b.def: the state where the one watching and the thing watched stop being two
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'flow state'. Flow keeps a self who is enjoying it; samadhi does not.

tier_b.def: a power that shows up as a by-product of long practice
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'ability'. An ability is trained for directly; a siddhi arrives sideways and is not the goal.

tier_b.def: love used as the method itself, not as a feeling about the method
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'devotion' when the love is the technique, not the decoration on top of it.

tier_b.def: losing your appetite for what used to pull you, without hating it
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'detachment'. Detachment is a decision you make; vairagya is an appetite that cooled on its own.

tier_b.def: knowledge that changes the knower, not information he holds
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'knowledge' when knowing the thing rearranges the person.

tier_b.def: power as a living, willing, feminine principle, the doing side of the divine
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'energy' or 'power' when the power has a will of its own and can be addressed.

tier_b.def: a place built around one practice and one teacher, where people live
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'retreat'. A retreat is a booking; an ashram is a household with a rule.

tier_b.def: one who saw a mantra rather than composed it
tier_b.when: Use instead of 'sage'. A sage thought his way to wisdom; a rishi received it and only passed it on.

rejected_note: Cut from 649 candidates down to 158 keepers. Rejected in groups: (1) SUBJECT WORDS, not voice - the meditation family (meditation, meditate, meditating, meditative, mindfulness, mindful, concentration, contemplation, contemplative, stillness, alertness, attentiveness, restlessness), chanting/chant/recitation/visualization/posture/breathing and the breath set (inhale, exhale, inhalation, exhalation, nostril, nasal, plexus), and the abstraction set (consciousness, transcendental, formless, oneness, macrocosm, microcosm, psychical, sentient-adjacent metaphysics, duality, causal, primordial). These are frequent only because of what the books are about; borrowing them makes a 21-year-old sound like he is quoting. (2) MEDICAL AND AYURVEDIC JARGON - alkalosis, acidosis, sacral, phlegm, mucus, saliva, digestion, digestive, indigestion, undigested, heartburn, acidity, acidic, detoxification, constipation, enema, asthmatic, excitatory, inhibitory, glandular, neurotransmitters, disequilibrium, plus the dosha set (vata, pitta, kapha, dosha, dhatus, humours) - all clustered in one or two books and zero use in the 2024 books. (3) PROPER NOUNS AND MYTHOLOGY - garuda, drona, vira, raja, empress, chariot, discus, trident-as-weapon, dynasty, clan, coronation, plus Hindi fragments the tokenizer kept (mein, kara, puri). (4) OCR NOISE from the scans - erings, erent, ering, ered, erence, ngers, nger, orts, speci, cation, ifyou, at's, limbed, passbook. (5) ARCHAIC OR STIFF - aforesaid, verily, henceforth, yore, olden, thrice, salutation, benediction, expiation, oblation, libation, prostration, consecrate. He can read these; writing them in 2026 reads as costume. (6) LIMP ABSTRACT NOUNS built from adjective + -ness, which are the exact opposite of vivid - restlessness, sluggishness, dullness, laziness, tiredness, heaviness, calmness, sharpness, fearlessness, thoughtlessness, possessiveness, negativity, positivity, oneness. (7) ALREADY EVERYDAY, so they teach nothing - mere, gently, softly, profound, subtle, sacred, divine, blessed, discipline, emotion, gratitude, forgiveness, sadness, jealousy, hatred, empathy, destiny, essence. (8) NUMERALS AND ORDINALS that only rank high because of counted practices - forty, fourteen, sixteen, eleventh, twelfth, fifteenth, sixteenth. (9) WORD-FAMILY DUPLICATES, collapsed to the single most useful form - purify/purification/purity/impure/impurity, effortless/effortlessly, eternal/eternally, contented/contentment, incessant/incessantly, unfailing/unfailingly, agreeable/disagreeable. (10) NEAR MISSES that were good but lost the cut for space or overlap - excruciating, deafening, bustling, coursing, searing, untold, swayed, illusory, gratification, deliberation, befitting, auspicious, dunce, pauper, elated, dejected, dismayed, bookish, sanctum, equipoise, aspirant, arduous, myriad, oblivious, ephemeral, respite, tenacity, futility, predicament, morsel. Any of these can be promoted into Tier A later without changing the shape of the list. SOURCING NOTE: Tier A is drawn from cands.txt and cands_late.txt, except quietude (32 uses, 9 books), askance (4/4), hanker (4/3) and frugally (4/3), which the brief named as targets but which sit below the top-400 cut; all four were verified in the corpus lexicon at lex_all.json. Tier B could not come from the two input files at all - lexicon.py strips every Indic term with its is_indic filter before writing them - so Tier B was rebuilt from lex_all.json, and every term listed carries its real corpus count and book spread. Tier C likewise pulls ghee, deodar, tulsi, lentils, sweetmeat, earthen, embers, firepit, hermitage and pebble from lex_all.json, since concrete nouns score low on the voice metric that produced the top 400.
